---
title: "Report-style figure"
description: "Combine several plots in one Matplotlib grid for a report."
date: 2026-01-13
categories: [customisation, subplots]
tags: [Visualizations]
---

```{python}
#| label: fig-report-figure
#| fig-alt: "Report figure combining scatter, density and per-location panels"
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import soundscapy as sspy

data = sspy.isd.load_demo()

places = ["CamdenTown", "PancrasLock", "MarchmontGarden"]
report = data[data["LocationID"].isin(places)]

fig = plt.figure(figsize=(15, 10))
fig.suptitle("Soundscape analysis: comparing urban locations", fontsize=16, y=0.98)
gs = fig.add_gridspec(2, 2, height_ratios=[1, 1.2])

ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0])
sspy.scatter(report, title="All locations - scatter", hue="LocationID", diagonal_lines=True, ax=ax1)

ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 1])
sspy.density(
    report,
    title="All locations - density",
    hue="LocationID",
    density_type="simple",
    incl_scatter=False,
    fill=False,
    diagonal_lines=True,
    ax=ax2,
)

ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, :])
ax3.axis("off")
n = len(places)
for i, place in enumerate(places):
    subax = ax3.inset_axes([i / n, 0, 1 / n, 1])
    sspy.iso_plot(
        report[report["LocationID"] == place],
        title=place,
        plot_layers=["scatter", "simple_density"],
        diagonal_lines=True,
        ax=subax,
    )
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
